## Body

**Security: block** at `a0ec95212431b8c12bbd7c477547a5242c8f78c0`.

S153-001 remains open: the new activity capability can be retrieved through victim re-registration.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs | 1066-1083 | Victim re-registration returns its context grant, enabling forged context reports | 10/10 |

An authenticated local caller can obtain a live Copilot victim's seat, session, pane and process incarnation from the ordinary roster, submit those identifiers to `/v1/register` with `native_extension_delivery: true`, and receive the victim's standing `context_token`. Native admission observes the supplied host and pane ancestry, but does not independently establish that the observed host sent this request (`registration.rs:575-650`). Same-incarnation registration returns the existing grant (`reported_context.rs:76-79`). The caller can then send a forged victim context report accepted by `/v1/activity` (`http/fyi.rs:257-289`), bypassing cold-wake protection or forging large-seat alerts.

Bind grant issuance/retrieval to independently authenticated reporting-seat provenance. Add a cross-caller regression that registers using correct victim identifiers and then attempts activity. The current activity regression seeds the grant directly and does not cover that issuance boundary.

The other repairs hold in source: missing/wrong grants refuse size reports before activity/context mutation; grants are memory-only, absent from roster/spine, and rotate with incarnation. Folder/seat command words use `shell_word`. The digest remains confined to the dormant PA wake. These controls do not close grant retrieval.

**Proof:** exact-head CI [42368571461](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42368571461), attempts 1 and 2, succeeded. Attempt-2 JUnit lists 2,079 passing cases, including the grant and activity cases. Source review, not locally executed exploit proof. No local builds/tests, credential reads, product changes or live fleet probes.

Public-content review found no credential disclosure in the reviewed changed material. Lockfile resolved sources remain exclusively `registry.npmjs.org`, with the seven-day npm quarantine retained. Historical scrubbing, global notification atomicity and deployment proof are not claimed.
